questions.explanation: Lateral rotation about 45°.

questions.question: A therapist reviews the medical record of a patient with a peripheral nerve injury. The most common site for an ulnar never is the:

options.C: Superficial surface of the flexor retinaculum

questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve is most often injured behind the medial epicondyle.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In addition to therapeutic intervention, the therapist should also do:
questions.explanation: Therapists should also document and counsel patients.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The mitral valve of the heart controls the:

options.A: The amount of the blood from left. Atrium to the left. Ventricle
options.B: The amount of the blood from left. Atrium to the right. Ventricle
options.C: The amount of the blood from left. Ventricle to the right. Ventricle
options.D: The amount of the blood to pulmonary artery

questions.explanation: The mitral valve controls flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A therapist develops a physical therapy problem list after competing an initial examination on a patient diagnosed with right shoulder impingement. Which of the following entries would not typically belong in the physical therapy problem list?

options.A: Decreased active right shoulder lateral rotation
options.B: Decreased strength of the right upper trapezius and middle deltoid
options.C: Increased pain with right shoulder active movement
options.D: Increased stress secondary to financial problems

questions.explanation: Financial stress is not a physical therapy problem-list item for shoulder impingement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A physical therapist palpates the muscle bellies of the wrist extensors. The therapist follows the muscles proximally to their common origin. This bony landmark is termed the:
questions.explanation: The wrist extensors arise from the lateral epicondyle.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The ratio of chest compression to manual ventilation for a single rescuer in CPR is:
questions.explanation: Single-rescuer CPR in older guidelines used 15 compressions to 2 breaths.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: When two opposite phases are contained in a single pulse, the wave form is termed as:
questions.explanation: A pulse with two opposite phases is biphasic.

questions.question: A physical therapist conducts an initial examination on a patient diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Which of the following clinical findings would you expect the therapist to identify?
questions.explanation: Cogwheel rigidity is characteristic of Parkinson's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: An 18-year-old female diagnosed with left-sided congestive heart failure is referred to physical therapy. Which objective finding is most commonly associated with left-sided heart failure?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary oedema is the typical finding of left-sided heart failure.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The storage form of glucose in animals is:
questions.explanation: Stored mainly in the liver and muscle.

questions.question: The commonest cause of bacterial meningitis in adults is:
questions.explanation: Neisseria meningitidis in young adults.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Mallet finger is produced in which of the following injuries?

options.A: Avulsion of extensor tendon at the base of middle phalanx
options.B: Avulsion of flexor profundus tendon at the base of terminal phalanx
options.C: Avulsion of extensor tendon at the base of terminal phalanx

questions.explanation: Mallet finger is avulsion of the extensor tendon at the base of the terminal phalanx.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which test is concerned with tennis elbow?
questions.explanation: Cozen's test (resisted wrist extension) is used for tennis elbow.

questions.question: The frequency of infrasonic waves lie between:
questions.explanation: Infrasound is below 20 Hz.

questions.question: A therapist conducts reflex testing on a patient with a traumatic brain injury. Which stimulus should the therapist utilize to test for clonus at the ankle?

options.C: Passive, rapid dorsiflexion of the ankle
options.D: Passive, slow dorsiflexion of the ankle

questions.explanation: Clonus at the ankle is elicited by a rapid passive dorsiflexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Gower's sign is apparent during which of following position?
questions.explanation: Gowers' sign is seen when rising from sitting or lying to standing.

questions.question: Which of the following exercise would be inappropriate for a woman who gave birth via cesarean section two days ago?
questions.explanation: Partial sit-ups are inappropriate two days after caesarean section.
